cohort: The study included 94 women diagnosed with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) after 24 weeks of gestation, excluding those with multiple gestations, pre-existing diabetes, or chronic comorbidities.
finding: Women with GDM requiring insulin therapy exhibited higher BMI and trends toward greater maternal and neonatal complications compared with diet-treated women, with preterm birth and macrosomia emerging as the most significant determinants of adverse neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean deliveries were higher among women with GDM requiring insulin therapy (57.89%) compared to those managed with diet alone (42.86%).
birth_weight: Mean birth weight was 3.26 +/- 0.46 kg in the insulin group and 3.02 +/- 0.42 kg in the diet group; birth weight >=3.5 kg was identified as an independent predictor of NICU admission.
gest_age: GDM was diagnosed after 24 weeks of gestation, and preterm delivery was identified as an independent predictor of adverse neonatal outcomes.
